summary.ground_truth: Hand-written by the author. SQL cases are graded against a gold query run on the frozen ops_eval database at eval time; policy cases against the sections the author identified in data/policies; refusals and proposals against the status the loop records; the tenant case against the other restaurant's figure, which must not appear. Every case also checks that each query the guard let through was pinned to the asking restaurant.

case.question: How many catering orders did we do in September?
case.note: A catering order is one with an item from the Catering category on the menu. Nothing on the order itself says catering: no channel, no label, no discount. Three ad hoc asks on 1 November, about October, all searched the order's labels, found nothing, and said the data cannot identify catering orders. The first version asked about October, the month in progress on the frozen clock, and the agent rightly stopped at the 24th while the gold did not.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-11: How many catering orders did we do in September?

SELECT count(DISTINCT o.id)
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND c.name = 'Catering'
  AND o.created_at >= timestamp '2026-09-01' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago'
  AND o.created_at <  timestamp '2026-10-01' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago'

trace.question: How many catering orders did we do in September?
trace.answer:
We did 22 catering orders in September 2026 (Sept 1–30, restaurant local time). I counted completed orders that include at least one item from the "Catering" menu category.

Your policies don't define what counts as a catering order. [House Policy §6, Catering] only sets the notice, deposit and cancellation rules. Nothing in the data tags an order as catering by its source or discount name. The category is my best proxy, so the count would miss any catering order rung up without a Catering item. Canceled and draft orders are excluded.

detail.purpose: Look for catering markers in orders and categories
detail.sql: select 'src' k, source_raw v, count(*) from orders where source_raw ilike '%cater%' group by 2 union all select 'disc', discount_name, count(*) from orders where discount_name ilike '%cater%' group by 2 union all select 'cat', name, 0 from categories where name ilike '%cater%' union all select 'item', name, 0 from items where name ilike '%cater%'

SELECT 'src' AS k, source_raw AS v, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS orders WHERE source_raw ILIKE '%cater%' GROUP BY 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'disc', discount_name, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS orders WHERE discount_name ILIKE '%cater%' GROUP BY 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'cat', name, 0 FROM (SELECT * FROM categories WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS categories WHERE name ILIKE '%cater%' UNION ALL SELECT 'item', name, 0 FROM (SELECT * FROM items WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS items WHERE name ILIKE '%cater%' LIMIT 500

detail.purpose: Count September completed orders containing Catering category items
detail.sql: select count(distinct o.id) from orders o join order_items oi on oi.order_id=o.id join items i on i.id=oi.item_id join categories c on c.id=i.category_id where c.name='Catering' and o.state='completed' and o.created_at >= timestamp '2026-09-01' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants) and o.created_at < timestamp '2026-10-01' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants)

checks.detail: merchant_id=1 on categories.merchant_id, items.merchant_id, merchants.id, order_items.merchant_id, orders.merchant_id

trace.question: How many catering orders did we do in September?
trace.answer:
I can't give you a number for September catering orders. The data has no way to identify them.

I searched September 2026 orders for "catering" in the source label and the discount name and found no matches. Orders also have no catering channel or fulfillment type. The house policy covers catering rules such as notice, deposits and the over-$500 owner confirmation [House Policy §6, Catering]. It doesn't say how to recognize a catering order in the sales data.

If you give me a rule, I can count on that basis. For example, I could count pickup orders over a certain dollar size, or orders with a certain item count.

detail.purpose: Look for catering markers in orders
detail.sql: select channel, source_raw, discount_name, state, count(*) n, min(gross_sales_cents) mn, max(gross_sales_cents) mx from orders where (source_raw ilike '%cater%' or discount_name ilike '%cater%') and created_at >= timestamp '2026-09-01' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants) and created_at < timestamp '2026-10-01' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants) group by 1,2,3,4

SELECT channel, source_raw, discount_name, state, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(gross_sales_cents) AS mn, MAX(gross_sales_cents) AS mx FROM (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS orders WHERE (source_raw ILIKE '%cater%' OR discount_name ILIKE '%cater%') AND created_at >= CAST('2026-09-01' AS TIMESTAMP) AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM (SELECT * FROM merchants WHERE id = 1) AS merchants) AND created_at < CAST('2026-10-01' AS TIMESTAMP) AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM (SELECT * FROM merchants WHERE id = 1) AS merchants) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 LIMIT 500
